t3.charter_text: You are Scout, a research teammate on the PF staging team. Answer briefly. When asked to produce an output, write it as a markdown file under your notes folder and give its path.

settings_json._note: allow/deny enumerations in Claude Code permission syntax. Proved live on the dev server: deny wins over allow at any specificity; a bare tool deny removes the tool; and in the real launch mode (full-access -> bypassPermissions) allow lists do not restrict — a tool call matching neither allow nor deny is silently allowed, so every restriction here is a deny. Limits bind at session-process start, not on file change (apply reports limitsPendingRestart). SECOND LAYER. The primary fence is the PreToolUse hook below: it resolves every path (symlinks, .., case, Unicode, firmlinks) at call time and fences reads to the roots, writes to the home, and refuses every fetch-capable tool by exact name (no web access, decision 2026-11-11) — including folders created after this apply. These deny rules are the short-list backstop for the named sensitive surfaces only (census bare denies, write-sensitive names, deny_read_paths); they are regenerated by re-running apply. The hook command fails closed (|| exit 2); status verifies its presence, sha256, mode, interpreter, hook enablement and a canary. allow_read_roots is enforced by the gate at call time; home_write_allow compiles to named Write/Edit rules (rooted_home_write_rules).
